card.name: Words introducing a drug combination
card.fires_on: The word just before a drug name in interaction text, such as 'receiving', 'taking', or 'of' after 'concomitant use' or 'co-administration'. It also fires inside a drug name just before 'taken in conjunction with'.

modes.label: Patients receiving/taking
modes.description: Verb after 'patients' that leads into a named drug given together with another.
modes.example: Monitor renal function periodically in patients<< receiving>> hydrochlorothiazide, losart

modes.label: Concomitant use of
modes.description: 'of' after 'concomitant use' or 'co-administration', before the drugs combined.
modes.example: Avoid concomitant use<< of>> esomeprazole magnesium

modes.label: Inside a drug name
modes.description: Partway through a drug name in a sentence about taking it together with another drug.
modes.example: The half-life of midazolam increased from 5 to 7 hours when<< mid>>azolam was taken in conjunction with

card.writes: It prepares words meaning combining or using together, such as 'combination' and 'combine'.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a drug interaction sentence where a second drug taken together is about to be named.
